title: Cyrus and the Bell
premise: Late-night radio host Jonah Vasquez starts receiving calls from listeners who died the previous week, and he keeps broadcasting to them because answering feels like a duty he cannot name. When an excavation crew beneath the old Bell Theater unearths a door sealed from the inside, something answers Jonah's signal and walks up through the phone lines wearing the voices of his dead callers. Trapped in the station until sunrise with his producer Dee and a grieving caller named Marcus, Jonah discovers the entity was invited decades ago by the station's founder, who bound it with a recorded confession. To survive, Jonah must broadcast that confession at full power before dawn, sacrificing his own voice — and the identity he built on air — to send it back through the door.
about_author: Rafael Coldharbour is the pen name of a former overnight radio engineer who spent six years alone in windowless studios and never quite stopped talking to the dead air. They write horror about people who mistake their jobs for their souls.

chapters.title: Dead Air, Live Callers
chapters.summary: Jonah hosts 'The Night Line' when a call comes in from Mrs. Okafor — whose obituary ran three days ago. He takes her call anyway, gentle and professional, while his hands shake. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: eerie tenderness; documentation as prayer begins.

chapters.title: The Logbook
chapters.summary: Jonah records every call from the dead in a leather logbook, cataloguing seven voices so far. Producer Dee finds the book and, instead of calling him crazy, adds her own annotations. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: found family flickers; two lonely people choosing belief over sanity.

chapters.title: Excavation at Bell Street
chapters.summary: Local news covers the dig beneath the condemned Bell Theater, where crews hit a steel door sealed from the inside. That night, a new caller — a man who died last week — whispers about the door being open now. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: dread arrives; the past surfaces.

chapters.title: Voices in Rotation
chapters.summary: The dead callers begin referencing each other, conversations Jonah never aired. One asks him to pass a message to Marcus Reyes, a living listener grieving his brother. Jonah visits Marcus, who begs him to keep the line open. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: love against duty — connection vs. safety.

chapters.title: What the Founder Recorded
chapters.summary: Digging into station archives, Dee finds a 1961 reel labeled only 'CONFESSION — DO NOT AIR,' made by founder Aldous Wren. The tape is missing its final minutes. POV: Dee. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into fear; the invitation revealed in fragments.

chapters.title: The Door Opens Inward
chapters.summary: Three excavation workers die overnight, all found facing the theater. On air, a new voice — not one of the dead callers — thanks Jonah for keeping the frequency warm. It knows his real name, which he has never said on air. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: violation; the watcher becomes the watched.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: A storm floods the streets; Jonah, Dee, and Marcus (who came seeking his brother's voice) are trapped in the station as phones ring from every dead line simultaneously. The building's exits lead back into the studio. POV: Marcus. Emotional beat: claustrophobia; strangers forced into family.

chapters.title: Rules of Broadcast
chapters.summary: The entity speaks through the board, explaining it can only enter where it is invited by voice. Every hour Jonah stays on air, it grows clearer. Dee discovers the studio's copper wiring was designed as a cage, not a transmitter. POV: Dee. Emotional beat: terrible understanding; the station itself is the trap.

chapters.title: Marcus's Brother
chapters.summary: The entity wears Marco Reyes's voice perfectly, offering Marcus absolution if he invites it in. Marcus nearly says yes; Jonah tackles the mic off the air, burning his hand on live equipment. POV: Marcus. Emotional beat: grief weaponized; love tested against manipulation.

chapters.title: Wren's Last Minutes
chapters.summary: In the flooded basement archive, Dee recovers the reel's ending: Wren didn't banish the thing — he married himself to it, trading his identity to hold the door shut from inside. His voice is still down there, still holding. POV: Dee. Emotional beat: horror and pity entwined; sacrifice as precedent.

chapters.title: The Hour of Static
chapters.summary: Power fails; the entity runs on generator hum, speaking through every speaker at once, offering each survivor their deepest want. Jonah almost accepts his dead mother's voice. Dee smashes the console to break the spell. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: temptation at its peak; identity under siege.

chapters.title: What Jonah Was Before
chapters.summary: Trapped in the dark, Jonah confesses to Dee and Marcus that 'Jonah Vasquez' is a broadcast persona; he came to this city erasing himself after a family tragedy. The entity feeds on dissolved identities — which is why it chose him. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: raw vulnerability; naming the wound.

chapters.title: Sunrise Math
chapters.summary: Dee calculates they have four hours until dawn, but the entity is accelerating the night — clocks run backward in the building. Marcus realizes his brother's true voice is still faintly on the dead lines, fighting the impostor. POV: Marcus. Emotional beat: desperate hope; time as antagonist.

chapters.title: The Confession Plan
chapters.summary: They reconstruct Wren's plan: airing the full confession at maximum wattage will rebind the entity, but the broadcaster must lend it their own voice as anchor — permanently. Jonah volunteers before anyone else can speak. POV: Dee. Emotional beat: love against duty inverted; she must let him go.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for the End
chapters.summary: They splice the reel, rig the transmitter past its limits, and rehearse. The entity, sensing the plan, plays back recordings of Jonah's best broadcasts — the nights he saved suicidal callers — asking who will save them when he's gone. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: doubt as siege engine; worth weighed.

chapters.title: Betrayal on the Board
chapters.summary: The entity seizes the automation system, cutting the transmitter feed and offering Dee her estranged daughter's voice if she stops Jonah. She pretends to negotiate, buying seconds, then restores power with bleeding fingers. POV: Dee. Emotional beat: loyalty proven under torture of the heart.

chapters.title: On Air, Forever
chapters.summary: 3:12 a.m. Jonah opens the mic and reads Wren's confession in his own voice, threading between the entity's screams. The dead callers join in, a chorus of the week's dead holding the frequency steady. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: climax; communion, courage, dissolution beginning.

chapters.title: The Door Sealed From Inside
chapters.summary: As the confession peaks, the basement door slams; the entity drags Jonah toward the studio's inner wall, where a second door has appeared. He walks in willingly, trading places with Wren's remnant, and the wall goes silent. POV: Marcus. Emotional beat: awe and devastation; the sacrifice completed.

chapters.title: Dawn, Off Air
chapters.summary: Sunrise. The station is ordinary again, scorched consoles and all. Dee and Marcus find the logbook's final page filled in Jonah's handwriting: instructions, frequencies, and one line — 'keep taking the calls.' POV: Dee. Emotional beat: grief braided with inheritance.

chapters.title: The New Night Line
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Dee and Marcus relaunch the show together, honoring the dead without opening doors. Calls come only from the living now, though sometimes static shapes a familiar cadence. POV: Marcus. Emotional beat: healing without forgetting; found family formalized.

chapters.title: Signal From the Other Side of the Wall
chapters.summary: During a test transmission, the board lights a channel that shouldn't exist. A voice like Jonah's, older and layered, reads the weather for a city that isn't theirs — then says goodnight to Dee by name. POV: Dee. Emotional beat: bittersweet coda; he endures, changed.

chapters.title: Cyrus and the Bell
chapters.summary: Final chapter reveals the title's meaning via Wren's recovered journal: Cyrus was the first host who answered the bell, and every generation someone must ring it back. Dee hangs a small brass bell by the studio door, ringing it each night at sign-off. POV: omniscient. Emotional beat: myth-making closure; the vigil continues.
